The Black Prince, also known as Edward of Woodstock, was the eldest son of King Edward III of England and was born on June 15, 1330. He was given the nickname "The Black Prince" although the reason for this name is not definitively known. Some historians suggest it might have been due to the color of his armor or the black shield he carried, which bore the royal arms of England.

The Black Prince is best known for his military prowess and his role in the Hundred Years' War between England and France. He was a key figure in several significant battles, including the Battle of Crécy in 1346, where he fought alongside his father, and the Battle of Poitiers in 1356, where he captured King John II of France. His victory at Poitiers was a major turning point in the war, leading to the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360.

Despite his military successes, the Black Prince did not become king. He died on June 8, 1376, before his father, and was succeeded by his ten-year-old son, Richard II, who became king upon the death of Edward III in 1377.
